statement: Joining a storage directory and a file name, then splitting the result, gives back the same directory and the same file name.
witness: dirs = ["."], leading = true, trailing = false, name = "a"
evidence: Test (shadow src/storage.rs mod proptests, joined_path_splits_back_into_its_parts) asserts storage::parent(join_path("/.", "a")) == Some("/.") as a string. join_path gives "/./a"; storage::parent is std::path::Path::new(path).parent() (src/storage.rs:31-38), and std documents that Path::components normalizes away interior "." ("Occurrences of . are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path"), so it returns "/". "/" and "/." name the same directory (Path::new("/.") == Path::new("/") is true). Nothing in vaultwarden promises textual round-trip; the only unit test (src/storage.rs:266) checks "data/rsa_key.pem". Real callers: CONFIG_FILE parent/file name (src/config.rs:24-33) and the RSA key directory used as the opendal Fs root (src/config.rs:1701, src/auth.rs:77); the child is always a literal ("config.json", "rsa_key", ...). A "." reaches them only via an admin-set DATA_FOLDER such as "." or "/data/."; both still resolve to the same directory and file name (see reproduction). The test's generator also produces names "."/"..", for which Path::file_name returns None, but no caller passes such names.
reproduction: A scratch crate (functions copied verbatim from vaultwarden 64ae55c): join_path("/.","a") = "/./a"; parent = Some("/"); file_name = Some("a"); Path eq("/.", "/") = true. DATA_FOLDER="." -> parent "."; "/data/." -> parent "/data", file_name "config.json".
impact: None. The returned string differs, but it names the same directory, and the file name is correct. Upstream main (HEAD 64ae55c on 2026-10-30, i.e. the trial commit) has the same src/storage.rs. Unrelated to the witness: DATA_FOLDER="/" makes join_path return a relative "config.json" (base trimmed to empty), so data would be written relative to the working directory. The property's generator never produces a bare "/" base, so this was not the reported failure and was not triaged further.

statement: Rewriting JSON keys to start lower-case keeps every value and the same number of keys in every object, at every depth.
evidence: The behavior is real. process_json_key (src/util.rs:701-707) maps every case variant of "ssn" to "ssn", and otherwise lowercases only the first character, so distinct keys like SSN/Ssn/ssn or Name/name map to the same key. The later insert into serde_json::Map (a BTreeMap, since preserve_order is not enabled) silently overwrites the earlier one. Where it runs: (a) LowerCase<Value> (src/util.rs:640-698) on stored cipher data, fields and password history in Cipher::to_json (src/db/models/cipher.rs:196, 227, 255), and on send data (send.rs:148, 181); (b) the org export (src/api/core/organizations.rs:3053-3054) over server-generated to_json output. That output already has canonical camelCase keys, so collisions cannot occur there. The stored cipher type data is the client's login/card/identity/... object taken as a raw serde_json::Value (src/api/core/ciphers.rs:289-299, 542-572) and saved verbatim. So an authenticated client that sends an object with two keys differing only in first-letter case (or any two case variants of ssn) gets one of them back on every read. Bitwarden's cipher schema has no fields that differ only in case. Official clients send camelCase keys with encrypted string values, and every update replaces cipher.data wholesale, so legacy PascalCase and new keys are never merged into one row. The "SSN" special case exists to map legacy keys to "ssn", which presumes only one spelling per object. Case-insensitive key folding cannot be injective, and nothing documents that colliding keys are preserved. The test generator deliberately draws keys from [aAbBsS]{1,3}|SSN|Ssn to force collisions.
reproduction: Same scratch crate (convert_json_key_lcase_first, process_json_key, lcase_first copied verbatim): {"SSN":null,"Ssn":null} -> {"ssn":null}; {"Name":1,"SSN":"2.BBB|enc-b","name":2,"ssn":"2.AAA|enc-a"} -> {"name":2,"ssn":"2.AAA|enc-a"} (2 of 4 values dropped, no error).
impact: Only reachable through schema-violating cipher payloads that no Bitwarden client produces. The account owner (or an org member who can edit the cipher) would have to write both keys themselves. The row in the database keeps both values; only the API response loses one. The values are end-to-end encrypted and the client ignores unknown keys, so there is no cross-user effect and nothing to disclose. A client that sent such a payload would see one value silently replaced. Upstream main (HEAD 64ae55c, same as the trial commit) has identical src/util.rs and src/db/models/cipher.rs. This becomes real-live only if some client or importer is shown to emit case-variant duplicate keys.
